Environment tag on every event. Defaults to `production` under
`TANKOVAULT_PROFILE=production` and `development` otherwise.

Release tag on every event; defaults to the workspace version the binary was built
from, which is what makes a regression attributable to a deploy.

Host tag on every event. Left unset, Sentry reports none: the hostname of a replica is
infrastructure detail that [`Self::send_default_pii`] would otherwise gate.

Fraction of captured events actually sent, `0.0`-`1.0`. A blunt volume cap — it drops
whole issues, not repetitions of one — so leave it at `1.0` unless quota forces it.

Fraction of traces this service **starts** that are recorded, `0.0`-`1.0`.

`0.0` (the default) means it starts none of its own. It does **not** mean this service
is absent from a trace: a request or a broker message arriving with a trace already
sampled is continued regardless, which is what keeps one reader action readable across
the whole tier rather than ending at the first service configured differently. Set it
uniformly anyway — `0.05`-`0.2` is an ordinary production figure — since the service
that *starts* a trace is the one whose rate decides whether it exists at all.
Least severe `tracing` level reported as a Sentry **issue**.

Least severe `tracing` level kept as a **breadcrumb** — the trail attached to the next
issue. Records at or above [`Self::capture_level`] become issues instead.
How many breadcrumbs one event carries.
Attach a stack trace to events that carry none of their own.

Send personally identifying data with every event: the client IP, the full request
header set (`Authorization` and `Cookie` included) and the resolved user.

**Off, and worth leaving off.** A reader's IP address and session cookie are exactly
what a crash report does not need in order to be actionable, and Sentry is a third
party for the purposes of the data policy this deployment publishes. On, it also
widens what the HTTP middleware records, because `sentry-tower` reads this same flag
to decide whether to redact sensitive headers.

Record request spans through the shared HTTP stack: one Sentry transaction per
request, named by the *matched route* rather than the URI, so an id in the path does
not become its own transaction name.

Whether a started transaction is *kept* is [`Self::traces_sample_rate`]'s decision.
This is the switch for a service that should stay out of traces entirely.

Copy `tracing` span fields onto the Sentry span as attributes. Off: span fields in
this workspace routinely carry ids and user-supplied titles, and a transaction is
stored under a longer retention than a log line.
How long process exit waits for queued events to drain.
Print the SDK's own diagnostics to stderr. For proving a DSN works, not for running.

HS256 signing key for access tokens; wrapped in `SecretString` so a `tracing::debug!(?cfg)`
on this Debug-deriving, nested struct can't publish the key that authenticates every session.

Server-side password pepper: mixed into every argon2id hash so a leak alone can't be
brute-forced offline. Empty (default) is un-peppered, for compatibility with old
hashes; once configured it must stay stable or passwords stop verifying.

How long an access token stays valid. Short, because nothing revokes one before it
expires; the refresh token is the revocable half.

How long a refresh token stays valid, and so how long a signed-out-of-sight session can
come back. Each use rotates the token and revokes its predecessor.

Mark the refresh cookie `Secure`.

Defaults to true — a `bool`'s implicit default is `false`, which would silently send a
30-day refresh credential over plain HTTP.

Also selects the cookie's name/path (`__Host-` vs unprefixed), since a `__Host-`
cookie without `Secure` is refused by the browser. Flipping this forces one re-login.

Public origin of the web app, for passkeys — `https://tanko.example.com`.

Cannot be inferred from a request: `Host` is attacker-controlled, and trusting it
would let anyone mint credentials under a domain of their choosing. Unset falls back
to [`tankovault_config::EmailConfig::base_url`] and disables only passkeys.

Relying-party id: the registrable domain credentials are bound to. Defaults to

subdomains and keys must survive the move.
The name the authenticator shows in its prompt ("Save a passkey for …"); purely cosmetic.

Base64 (standard alphabet) 32-byte key that seals TOTP secrets at rest.

routine operation, and deriving from it would silently invalidate every enrolled
authenticator app — the same class of failure as rotating `password_pepper` and
stranding the seeded admin. Unset disables TOTP enrolment only; security keys and
recovery codes are unaffected, since neither stores a symmetric secret.

enabled.description:
Initialise the Sentry client. `false` installs no client, no panic hook and no layer,
so every other key here is inert and nothing is sent anywhere.

environment.description:
Environment tag on every event. Defaults to `production` under
`TANKOVAULT_PROFILE=production` and `development` otherwise.

http_transactions.description:
Record request spans through the shared HTTP stack: one Sentry transaction per
request, named by the *matched route* rather than the URI, so an id in the path does
not become its own transaction name.

Whether a started transaction is *kept* is [`Self::traces_sample_rate`]'s decision.
This is the switch for a service that should stay out of traces entirely.

max_breadcrumbs.description: How many breadcrumbs one event carries.

release.description:
Release tag on every event; defaults to the workspace version the binary was built
from, which is what makes a regression attributable to a deploy.

sample_rate.description:
Fraction of captured events actually sent, `0.0`-`1.0`. A blunt volume cap — it drops
whole issues, not repetitions of one — so leave it at `1.0` unless quota forces it.

send_default_pii.description:
Send personally identifying data with every event: the client IP, the full request
header set (`Authorization` and `Cookie` included) and the resolved user.

**Off, and worth leaving off.** A reader's IP address and session cookie are exactly
what a crash report does not need in order to be actionable, and Sentry is a third
party for the purposes of the data policy this deployment publishes. On, it also
widens what the HTTP middleware records, because `sentry-tower` reads this same flag
to decide whether to redact sensitive headers.

server_name.description:
Host tag on every event. Left unset, Sentry reports none: the hostname of a replica is
infrastructure detail that [`Self::send_default_pii`] would otherwise gate.

shutdown_timeout_secs.description: How long process exit waits for queued events to drain.

span_attributes.description:
Copy `tracing` span fields onto the Sentry span as attributes. Off: span fields in
this workspace routinely carry ids and user-supplied titles, and a transaction is
stored under a longer retention than a log line.

traces_sample_rate.description:
Fraction of traces this service **starts** that are recorded, `0.0`-`1.0`.

`0.0` (the default) means it starts none of its own. It does **not** mean this service
is absent from a trace: a request or a broker message arriving with a trace already
sampled is continued regardless, which is what keeps one reader action readable across
the whole tier rather than ending at the first service configured differently. Set it
uniformly anyway — `0.05`-`0.2` is an ordinary production figure — since the service
that *starts* a trace is the one whose rate decides whether it exists at all.

service_name.description: Logical service name reported in traces/metrics.

worker_url.description: Where the admin console's provider dry-run is forwarded, no trailing slash.

env.name: RUST_LOG
env.docs: Verbosity, as `tracing` directives — `info`, `tankovault_api=debug,info`. Read by `EnvFilter::try_from_default_env`, which is consulted *before* `telemetry.log_filter` and wins over it when set.
